definitions.explanation: having to do something twice because it wasn't done properly the first time, resulting in unnecessary extra work

examples.japanese: {二度手間|にどでま}になった。
examples.english: I ended up having to do it twice.

examples.japanese: {確認|かくにん}を{怠|おこた}ると{二度手間|にどでま}になる。
examples.english: If you neglect to confirm, you'll end up doing it twice.

examples.japanese: {二度手間|にどでま}を{避|さ}けるため、{最初|さいしょ}から{丁寧|ていねい}にやる。
examples.english: To avoid doing it twice, do it carefully from the start.

notes:
{二度手間|にどでま} refers to the inefficiency of having to redo something.

KANJI BREAKDOWN:
- {二度|にど} (twice, two times)
- {手間|てま} (time and effort, labor)

USAGE:
- {二度手間|にどでま}になる (to end up doing something twice)
- {二度手間|にどでま}を{省|はぶ}く (to save unnecessary repeat work)
- {二度手間|にどでま}を{避|さ}ける (to avoid doing something twice)

COMMON CONTEXTS:
- Work efficiency discussions
- When explaining why careful preparation matters
- Advice about not rushing through tasks

RELATED EXPRESSIONS:
- {手間|てま}がかかる (to take time and effort)
- {無駄|むだ}な{労力|ろうりょく} (wasted effort)
- {骨折|ほねお}り{損|ぞん} (waste of effort)
